items.abstract: <jats:p>Vision-based multimodal learning has experienced rapid advancement through the integration of large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). In this review, we adopt a historical and task-oriented perspective to systematically examine the evolution of multimodal vision models from early visual-semantic embedding frameworks to modern instruction-tuned MLLMs. We categorize model developments across major architectural paradigms, including dual-encoder contrastive frameworks, transformer-based fusion architectures, and unified generative models. Further, we analyze their practical implementations across key vision-centric tasks such as image captioning, visual question answering (VQA), visual grounding, and cross-modal generation. Comparative insights are drawn between traditional multimodal fusion strategies and the emerging trend of large-scale multimodal pretraining. We also provide a detailed overview of benchmark datasets, evaluating their representativeness, scalability, and limitations in real-world multimodal scenarios. Building upon this analysis, we identify open challenges in the field, including fine-grained cross-modal alignment, computational efficiency, generalization across modalities, and multimodal reasoning under limited supervision. Finally, we discuss potential research directions such as self-supervised multimodal pretraining, dynamic fusion via adaptive attention mechanisms, and the integration of multimodal reasoning with ethical and human-centered AI principles. Through this comprehensive synthesis of past and present multimodal vision research, we aim to establish a unified reference framework for advancing future developments in visual-language understanding and cross-modal intelligence.</jats:p>
title: Vision–Language Foundation Models and Multimodal Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Benchmarks, and Open Challenges

items.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated strong potential in heuristic algorithm design, yet existing approaches are confined to text-only interactions and fail to exploit visual structure in optimization trajectories. We propose \textbf{VE-FWA} (Visual-Enhanced Fireworks Algorithm), a multimodal framework that incorporates visual feedback into LLM-driven evolution of the Fireworks Algorithm (FWA), governed by a \emph{Critical Part} (CP) abstraction that unifies global optimizer evolution and local subroutine customization. We validate VE-FWA on two challenging domains: the Traveling Salesman Problem (combinatorial optimization) and VLSI placement (high-dimensional physical design). On the full TSPLIB29 benchmark, VE-FWA achieves a 0.0038\% average optimality gap, reaching the known optimum on 25 out of 29 instances, while multimodal feedback reduces the gap by $54\times$ compared to the text-only variant. On EDA placement, VE-FWA achieves the best wirelength on 6 out of 8 ISPD2005 benchmarks using only a single 12\,GB GPU, outperforming prior LLM-based approaches that require large-scale compute clusters.</jats:p>
title: Visual-Enhanced Fireworks Algorithm via Multimodal Large Language Models
